sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully encodes the direct-static implication: exact A/B category, oil-tanker classification, deadweight below 5000 metric tonnes, and construction date on or after 2017-01-01 applicability; both ship-owned protection statuses are required to have exactly one xsd:boolean true value only when applicable. Targets, canonical terms, datatypes, unit, threshold directions, and non-applicable behavior are correct.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the conditional status checks: requiring that each status has at least one true value allows contradictory data containing both true and false to pass. Constrain each required ship-owned status to exactly one xsd:boolean value equal to true, or make the SPARQL violation query reject any applicable node having a non-true value as well as missing true evidence. Preserve the existing ship target, applicability conditions, threshold, and unit.

Repair the non-applicable oil-tanker alternative: the current SPARQL query selects shipType = oil_tanker, so it rejects oil tankers and allows non-oil tankers to satisfy the alternative. Make it select a present shipType value unequal to oil_tanker (while retaining minCount 1), or use an equivalent SHACL Core negation. Also represent the declared directConstraintTerm nltl:oilTanker on the required ship owner, using the supplied canonical class consistently with the ship_type applicability condition; do not omit this contract term. Preserve the exact A/B category, oil-tanker, deadweight < 5000, construction date >= 2017-01-01 applicability, metric-ton unit, and exactly-one-true status checks.

The conditional logic is still over-restrictive: the sh:or permits only applicable ships satisfying all applicability inputs and non-oil-tankers, so an oil tanker with category C, deadweight >= 5000, construction before 2017, or missing applicability evidence fails even though this requirement imposes no protection-status constraint on it. Encode implication instead: enforce the two exactly-one-true ship-owned status properties only when category is A or B, ship type is oil_tanker, deadweight is less than 5000 metric tonnes, and construction date is on or after 2017-01-01; all non-applicable ships must pass without those statuses. Preserve the supplied ship target, canonical oilTanker class representation on the ship, datatypes, metric-ton unit, threshold direction, and prior exact-one-true status instruction.

Candidate faithfully encodes the direct-static implication: exact A/B category, oil-tanker classification, deadweight below 5000 metric tonnes, and construction date on or after 2017-01-01 applicability; both ship-owned protection statuses are required to have exactly one xsd:boolean true value only when applicable. Targets, canonical terms, datatypes, unit, threshold directions, and non-applicable behavior are correct.
